channel.title: Deepgrain: People Ops AI
channel.description: Working notes on running People functions with AI.

item.title: The People Ops diagnostic toolkit
item.description: The read comes before the fix. The People Ops diagnostic toolkit is five repeatable diagnostics that tell you where a People function actually snags.

item.title: People debt: what GenAI exposes, and what to do about it
item.description: GenAI does not create people debt, it exposes it: drifting levelling, unowned decision rights, undocumented process. Here is the audit and the order to repay.

item.title: Designing values that stick
item.description: Most values projects produce a poster, not a behaviour. Values that stick are short, costly to live by, and wired into how decisions actually get made.

item.title: Coaching and feedback systems that actually compound
item.description: A review cycle is not a coaching system. Coaching and feedback systems that compound run weekly and evidence-led. Here is the shape, and where AI fits.

item.title: AI roadmap case study: FinEdge's first 90 days
item.description: An AI roadmap case study: how a 280-person fintech People team went from scattered ChatGPT use to nine production workflows in 90 days, and what nearly broke.

item.title: The HR Architect: a new role inside the People function
item.description: AI is climbing from clicks to decisions, and the People roles that survive change shape. The HR Architect is the role your function needs to build now.

item.title: The automation audit playbook
item.description: An automation audit done properly starts with the problem, not the tool. Score each workflow with 6T, cost it in pounds, then sequence by value.

item.title: An AI policy blueprint for People teams
item.description: Most AI policies ban everything and get ignored by day two. Here is the one-page AI policy for People teams people actually use, plus how to handle shadow AI.

item.title: Production agents for People Ops
item.description: Most People Ops agents are demos with ambition. Production agents for People Ops share a pattern: real data, a context stack, an off-switch, an owner.

item.title: An AI enablement operating model for People leaders
item.description: Champions and licences are not a strategy. AI enablement is an operating model with three layers and a cadence. How People leaders build one that sticks.

item.title: Choosing AI models for HR work
item.description: No single best AI model for HR work exists. Match the model to the task, run two or three, and cross-check what matters. Here is the working stack.

item.title: Prompting patterns for People Ops
item.description: Better AI output is not about a better model. It is about prompting patterns for People Ops: five blocks, prompt chains, and the critique pass teams skip.

item.title: AI workspace setup for People teams (Claude, ChatGPT, Copilot)
item.description: Your AI sounds generic because it works generically. Here is the AI workspace setup that turns Claude, ChatGPT or Copilot into a colleague that knows your team.

item.title: From prompts to systems
item.description: Buying tools or nudging people to use ChatGPT is not building AI capability. The move from prompts to systems has one order: workflows, automations, agents.

item.title: Designing the AI-native People team
item.description: Bolting AI onto the People org chart changes nothing but the bill. An AI-native People team is redesigned around it: fewer roles, more senior, work that stays.

item.title: AI governance for People teams
item.description: AI governance for People teams is not a forty-page policy. It is four boundaries, a sign-off, and a log. Here is what to decide, and how to prove it holds.

item.title: The champion model
item.description: You do not need engineers to build AI capability in People. You need a champion model: three or four operators given air cover, a budget and time. How it runs.

item.title: Leading the AI transformation in People
item.description: Leading the AI transformation in People fails as a change programme far more often than as a technology problem. Here is the sequence that actually sticks.

item.title: Diagnosing AI readiness in People Ops
item.description: AI readiness in People Ops is not a model problem. It is a data, process, tooling, sponsor and risk read. Here is the diagnostic, and how to act on it.

item.title: A workflow assessment framework for People Ops
item.description: Most People teams pick AI workflows by instinct or by what is loudest. A workflow assessment framework scores value, frequency, fit and risk into a plan you can defend.

item.title: Automation patterns that pay off
item.description: The payoff from People Ops automation patterns is not the clever model. It is the clean workflow. Six that pay back in weeks, and the ones that quietly die.

item.title: The People Ops AI domain map
item.description: A People Ops AI map: the five domains where AI fits across the People function, the shape of the win in each, and how to pick which one to build first.

item.title: Measuring AI value in People Ops
item.description: Time saved is the vanity metric every function reports and no CFO banks. Here is how measuring AI value in People Ops actually works, and how to defend it.
